title: codemother's seal teeth ask a tester on their own box
intention: CodeMother's seal teeth ask the tester's run verb of a bus on their own box, so the fixture path they send names a file that tester can read.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akienasus: CAIRN_BUS_HOME=akiendelllinux.local:7419, so reach('tester') asked the Dell's tester, which replied {refused: no proof file at '/home/akien/cairn/...'}; ['body']['record'] raised KeyError in 6 teeth of test_codemother.py, at import in test_clearance.py, and in test_codemother_proofs_ride_the_published_scratch_bus.py, which runs test_codemother.py.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof a peer leans on reads the same on every box) and RULE 1 (the tester is still asked through its run verb).
how: In each proof, _seal asks the run verb from a child (sys.executable <proof> --ask-run <path>) under one scratch HOME per proof process (scratch.home_env drops CAIRN_BUS_*); the child's reach lazy-inits a throwaway bus there and prints the reply on its last stdout line. atexit shuts that bus down with RemoteBus(<home>/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0).shutdown(). The 42ddfe3b7256 pattern.

clauses.claim: test_codemother.py is green on akienasus with CAIRN_BUS_HOME naming akiendelllinux
no scratch bus these proofs started is running after they exit

decisions.text: D1: test_codemother.py's _seal asks from a scratch-HOME child, one HOME per process, shut down at exit.
D2: test_clearance.py's _seal does the same, its own copy (RULE 1: no import across proofs of another component).

measured.saw: reply body {refused: no proof file at '/home/akien/cairn/cairn/devices/tester/proofs/fixtures/green_proof.py' — nothing was run and no verdict was read}
measured.how: reach('tester').request(verb='run', body={path: <green fixture>}) on akienasus under the session env

measured.saw: test_codemother 24/30, the 6 reds all KeyError 'record'; test_clearance KeyError at import; the scratch-bus proof red on test_codemother
measured.how: bin/cairn test over the 30 codemother candidates
